page: Microsoft Azure E64-16as_v5 is a constrained vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Cache allocations include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning is the defining characteristic of this configuration, offering 512.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an extensive 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng reaching 2713.09, ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core throughput aligns with expectations for a 16-thread slice, achieving 21619.81 on stress-ng and 9832.0 on Geekbench multi-core. PassMark memory testing registers a strong score of 2758.61, supported by cached read memory bandwidth of 1034.13 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached write throughput shows lower bandwidth at 22.79 GB/sec. For in-memory data structures, the configuration sustained 16.08 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 7023.9 on PassMark database operations.

The constrained CPU profile provides qualitative cost efficiency by maintaining the massive 512.0 GB RAM footprint of a larger host while reducing compute licensing overheads tied to core counts. The primary tradeoff is the lower core-to-memory density, alongside the lack of local temporary NVMe storage. Microsoft Azure E64-16as_v5 is optimal for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers like Redis, big data analytics engines, and workloads that require significant memory footprints without needing high parallel core capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16as_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It includes 512.0 GB of RAM, offering an unusually high ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 2713.09 and strong PassMark memory performance at 2758.61. General compute benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9832.0 and Redis SET throughput of 16.08 million ops/sec, display solid mid-tier capabilities. This constrained CPU configuration lowers per-core licensing expenses while preserving an immense RAM footprint, making it particularly well suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise Redis caching, and memory-bound transactional systems.
